objective: Avoid per-chunk heap-string allocation while hex-encoding bounded DXF binary payload chunks.

behavior: The vector-backed group-310 helper hex-encodes each at-most-127-byte chunk into a fixed 254-character stack buffer.
The helper passes a string_view limited to the populated hex characters to the synchronous writer and stops immediately when that write fails.
Chunk boundaries, uppercase hex, empty input, writer error state, payload ownership, and wire output are unchanged.
implementation.compatibility: Internal writer path only; no installed API, public class layout, or DRW_Interface callback changed.
implementation.scope_note: The separate std::string overload and manual OLE payload loops are unchanged.

controls: Generated AC1024 ASCII/Binary revolved-surface payloads assert exact 127/127/46-byte source chunk order as 254/254/92 uppercase hex characters.
The control verifies both declared group-90 values, unchanged caller bytes, and a following-record sentinel.
limits: Source-level allocation avoidance is established by the fixed stack buffer and synchronous string_view sink; allocator counts, peak RSS, and throughput were not measured.
The focused generated control exercises the common vector-backed group-310 helper. The std::string overload and independent OLE2/OLEFRAME loops remain separate paths.
No full suite, peer runtime, native CAD application, external drawing, or sanitizer/fuzz campaign was run.
